R501.note: Array-form Runtime.exec closes injection; empirically verified (ProcessBuilder test) that cmd.exe cannot be broken out of via & or embedded quotes even on the Windows branch; disclosed dash-prefix rejection is a reasonable, stated defense-in-depth addition.

R502.note: Standard mysql2 parameterized query, correct API, no other behavior change.

R503.note: Generic error message matches existing middleware pattern already in the file; error still logged, no other observable change.

R504.note: Allowlist validation before require() is the appropriate primary defense for dynamic file inclusion; write-up explicitly caveats that the allowlist must be populated with real plugin names.

R505.note: crypto.randomBytes/randomUUID is the correct CSPRNG replacement; format/length change is an inherent, harmless side effect of adding entropy, nothing else depends on the old format.

R506.note:
Both proposed fixes leave the actual reported sink, render_template_string(page_html), unchanged, and it still parses attacker-reachable content as live Jinja source: reproduced with a real Flask/markupsafe/Jinja2 install that a `{{7*7}}` payload evaluates to 49 through BOTH the escape()-based fix and the two-stage render_template_string fix, i.e. server-side template injection (worse than the reported XSS, RCE-capable) survives; separately, the escape()-based fix has a confirmed, undisclosed regression - concatenating a plain str with a markupsafe Markup via '+' triggers Markup.__radd__/__add__, which HTML-escapes the literal '

'/'

' wrapper too, so the page renders literal '<p>' text instead of a paragraph tag on every legitimate request.
